sections.title: The Haitian Revolution and the Atlantic World
sections.description: In 1791, enslaved plantation workers in the French colony of Saint Domingue rose up in a coordinated revolt, setting off a chain of events that resulted in the abolition of slavery and independence from France.  This course traces that history, focusing on the revolution’s significance as a site of cultural and ideological exchange in the revolutionary-era Atlantic world.  Events in Haiti propelled and were in turn shaped by political, economic and legal change in Europe, Africa, and the Americas more broadly.  Likewise, revolutionaries in Haiti understood events and made decisions by drawing on the colony’s complex mix of cultural and ideological influences: west and central west African, French, American, and creole.  We will pay special attention to the movement of people and ideas between Haiti and Philadelphia, incorporating hands-on work with original texts in the Kislak Center for Special Collections in the Van Pelt Library.
